summary: ansible-core 2.19 major changes: builtin Jinja filters/tests have ansible.builtin FQCNs, forks no longer inherit stdio (use Display), module_utils packages may have __init__.py, and the variable type system was formalized with native-type subclasses.
questions: Can I call Jinja builtin filters as ansible.builtin.<name>?
Why can't my controller plugin print to stdout from a worker?
Can module_utils packages contain __init__.py in ansible-test?
Why do I get errors storing custom Python objects in variables?

answer_card.title: ansible-core 2.19 major changes
answer_card.answer_md:
- **Jinja plugins:** builtin filters and tests are reachable as `ansible.builtin.<name>`.
- **Forks:** workers no longer inherit stdio; `stdout`, `stderr` and `stdin` are detached and non-functional. Controller-side plugins must use `Display`.
- **ansible-test:** packages under `module_utils` may contain `__init__.py`.
- **Variables:** the type system was overhauled; storing unsupported Python types gives earlier warnings or errors. Many values are subclasses of native types, which some libraries mishandle, so plugins may need to convert to native types.
